newsitem.title: USA: CHINA CROP SETBACKS MAY BOOST US EXPORTS--WEFA.
newsitem.headline: CHINA CROP SETBACKS MAY BOOST US EXPORTS--WEFA.

text.p: Downturns in China's corn and oilseed crops may create the opportunity for larger U.S. grain exports, a senior economist at WEFA Group said Tuesday.

In its monthly World Agricultural Supply and Demand Estimates report, the U.S. Agriculture Department lowered its forecast for China's corn crop by 12 million tonnes, to 110 million tonnes in 1996/97. Chinese exports were reduced to one million tonnes, half of July's forecast.

"I wouldn't be surprised to see that (export forecast) go down to zero," said WEFA senior ecnomist Mike Helmar, if difficulties continue. The Chinese crop has been hurt by widespread hot and dry weather.
U.S. sales to Asian markets could climb if Chinese corn is not available, Helmar said.

A smaller crop could have limited impact on China's imports, now forecast for 250,000 tonnes, he said. China has sizable stocks -- an estimated 41 million tonnes -- to buffer a short crop. In addition, imports levels will be "somewhat policy-driven."
Aside from Europe, most competitors in the world wheat market may see crop downturns, which will keep prices firm.
"It looks good for American wheat farmers," he said.
